newsitem.title: BOTSWANA: SADC SAYS MORE DEFECTIONS FROM RIVAL GROUP EXPECTED.
newsitem.headline: SADC SAYS MORE DEFECTIONS FROM RIVAL GROUP EXPECTED.

text.p: The Southern African Development Community (SADC) said on Tuesday it expected more defections of its members from the rival Common Market for East and Southern Africa (COMESA).
"I cannot say which way they will go, but we are expecting more member states to announce their position," SADC information officer Kgosinkwe Moesi told Reuters.
He said the SADC recently appealed to members, who hold joint membership of the trade groupings, to choose which organisation they wanted to belong to.
SADC members Mozambique and Lesotho announced their withdrawal from COMESA in December.
Of SADC's 12 members only Botswana and South Africa are not members of COMESA. Other SADC members are Angola, Malawi, Lesotho, Mozambique, Namibia, Swaziland, Tanzania, Zambia, Mauritius, Zimbabwe.
"There is no way both organisations can endeavour to establish a common market in southern Africa. That is unworkable." Moesi said.
"Now we are hopefully going to have a COMESA which comprises of non-SADC countries," he added.
It was however possible for both groups to cooperate, Moesi said.

"COMESA could restructure. In fact when the SADC summit took its decision it was envisaging a position where it would be easier for the two organisations to cooperate in a much more meaningful manner, persuing two different agendas.

"There are many (possible) levels of cooperation," he said. "SADC is working with so many other organisations and there is no reason why we should not find room for... I don't know what name you want to give it... COMESA.
"We could easily interact with east and central Africa through such an established block and in that way begin to see the reality of becoming one continental economic unit," Moesi said.
COMESA members include Angola, Malawi, Mauritius, Namibia, Swaziland, Tanzania, Zambia, Zimbabwe, Kenya, Uganda, Zaire, Burundi, Comoros, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Madagascar, Rwanda and Sudan.
